<P class="p1261 ft148">5.5.1. Issue 4: Extension to indirect owners</P>
<P class="p603 ft136"><SPAN class="ft119">75.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft147">The first issue is relevant in cases where the indirect owner is subject to a Covered Tax on the Hybrid Entity’s income. If Article 10.2.5 were limited to the direct owner, then any tax paid by the indirect owner would not be taken into account for the GloBE calculations in the jurisdiction where the Hybrid Entity is located. A further question would be whether such tax could be included in the GloBE calculations of the Parent Entity considering Articles 4.1.3(a) (which removes taxes related to income excluded from the GloBE calculations) and 4.3.3 (which requires taxes paid by a Parent Entity which cannot be allocated to a CFC or Hybrid Entity because of the passive income limitation to be kept in the parent jurisdiction).</SPAN></P>
<P class="p619 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">76.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">This is illustrated in the following example:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1262 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">77.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">In this example, A Co wholly owns B Co which in turn wholly owns C Co. A Co is located in Jurisdiction A, B Co in Jurisdiction B and C Co in Jurisdiction C. The table below summarises how each jurisdiction’s entity classification rules treat the entities.</SPAN></P>

<P class="p1053 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">78.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">Jurisdiction A regards both B Co and C Co as fiscally transparent entities. A Co is consequently subject to tax on C Co’s profits. As C Co is regarded as fiscally opaque in Jurisdiction C, it will also be subject to tax on its profits.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p589 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">79.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">Jurisdiction B’s tax laws do not treat C Co as a fiscally transparent entity. This means C Co will not meet the Hybrid Entity definition with respect to B Co. This would also be the case where Jurisdiction B does not have a Corporate Income Tax, and accordingly does not have tax laws, because in such cases Jurisdiction B will not treat C Co as a fiscally transparent entity. If the reference to owner in Article 10.2.5 is limited to the direct owner, this would prevent taxes paid by A Co on C Co’s profits from being allocated to C Co. This could result in double taxation if </SPAN><NOBR>top-up</NOBR> taxes are payable with respect to C Co. This could also result in an inflated ETR for Jurisdiction A if the tax is included in the ETR computation for Jurisdiction A as a result of not being allocated to C Co.</P>
<P class="p1264 ft116">TAX CHALLENGES ARISING FROM THE DIGITALISATION OF THE ECONOMY – ADMINISTRATIVE GUIDANCE ON THE GLOBAL <NOBR>ANTI-BASE</NOBR> EROSION MODEL RULES (PILLAR TWO), JUNE 2024 © OECD 2024</P>

<P class="p1127 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">80.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">Alternatively, if the reference to ‘owner’ in Article 10.2.5 includes an indirect owner, then C Co would be regarded as a Hybrid Entity because A Co is also subject to tax on its profits. This would allow any taxes paid by A Co with respect to these profits to be allocated to C Co under Article 4.3.2(d), which would prevent double taxation and be more consistent with the matching principle of the GloBE Rules.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p557 ft136"><SPAN class="ft119">81.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft147">The Inclusive Framework considers this is the more appropriate outcome and accordingly, the Commentary to Article 10.2.5 will be modified to clarify that the word “owner” refers to both the direct and indirect Constituent </SPAN><NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> of the Entity. Consequently, Covered Taxes reflected in the financial accounts of the direct and indirect Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owners</NOBR> that relates to the income of the Hybrid Entity and are imposed because the Entity is fiscally transparent under the tax law applicable to such direct and indirect Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owners</NOBR> will be allocated to the Hybrid Entity subject to the limitations in Article</P>
<P class="p1265 ft148">5.5.2. Guidance</P>
<P class="p595 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">82.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft154">The bold text will be added to paragraph 59 of the Commentary to Article 4.3.2(d):</SPAN></P>
<P class="p643 ft136"><SPAN class="ft119">59.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft147">Paragraph (d) allocates Taxes of </SPAN><SPAN class="ft201">direct and indirect </SPAN>Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owners</NOBR> arising in connection with the income of Hybrid Entities. If a Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> of a Hybrid Entity is located in a tax jurisdiction that imposes Tax on the owner’s share of the Hybrid Entity’s income under a fiscal transparency regime (see discussion in Commentary to Article 10.2), the Covered Taxes included in the financial accounts of the Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> should be assigned to the Hybrid Entity. The same general process described in paragraph (a) above for allocating Covered Taxes imposed on the Main Entity in respect of a PE can be used to determine the amount of taxes allocated by a Constituent Entity owner to a Hybrid Entity, however any taxes allocated to a Hybrid Entity by a Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> in respect of Passive Income are subject to limitation under Article 4.3.3, which is discussed further below. If the Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> is subject to a withholding tax or net basis taxes on distributions from the Hybrid Entity, such Taxes would also be allocated to the Hybrid Entity pursuant to paragraph (e).</P>
<P class="p1266 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">83.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft154">The following paragraphs will be added after paragraph 59 of the Commentary to Article 4.3.2(d):</SPAN></P>
<P class="p643 ft136"><SPAN class="ft128">59.1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft161">Article 4.3.2(d) allocates Covered Taxes included in the financial accounts of a direct and indirect Constituent </SPAN><NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> on the income of the Hybrid Entity to the Hybrid Entity. This means that Covered Taxes in the financial accounts of multiple Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owners</NOBR> having, directly or indirectly, the same Ownership Interests can be allocated to the Hybrid Entity.</P>
<P class="p671 ft119"><SPAN class="ft128">59.2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft160">For example, A Co is a tax resident in jurisdiction A which owns B Co, a tax resident in jurisdiction B, which owns C Co, a tax resident in jurisdiction C. The MNE Group owns no other Constituent Entities in jurisdiction C. A Co, B Co and C Co are not </SPAN><NOBR>Flow-through</NOBR> Entities.</P>
<P class="p822 ft136">Jurisdiction A treats B Co and C Co as fiscally transparent. Jurisdiction B also treats C Co as fiscally transparent. C Co’s profit is 100 which is composed only of active income and subject to a 10% tax in jurisdiction C (10 of tax). Jurisdiction B taxes C Co’s profit at a rate of 15% and provides a foreign tax credit such that B Co pays 5 of tax. Jurisdiction A also taxes C Co’s profit at a rate of 18% and provides a foreign tax credit for taxes paid in jurisdictions B and C such that A Co pays 3 of tax. The taxes paid by A Co and B Co are reflected in their financial accounts.</P>
<P class="p631 ft119"><SPAN class="ft128">59.3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft160">In this case, Article 4.3.2(d) will effectively allocate 5 of tax paid by B Co and 3 of tax paid by A Co to C Co because those taxes were paid in respect of C Co’s income. The Effective Tax Rate of jurisdiction C will be 18% ([10+5+3]/100).</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1267 ft116">TAX CHALLENGES ARISING FROM THE DIGITALISATION OF THE ECONOMY – ADMINISTRATIVE GUIDANCE ON THE GLOBAL <NOBR>ANTI-BASE</NOBR> EROSION MODEL RULES (PILLAR TWO), JUNE 2024 © OECD 2024</P>

<P class="p1261 ft148">5.5.3. Issue 5: Entities located in jurisdictions without a Corporate Income Tax</P>
<P class="p537 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">84.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">The second issue relates to when a Constituent Entity is located in a jurisdiction without a corporate income tax or another Covered Tax. Pursuant to the guidance in paragraph 34 of this document, such Entities cannot be considered fiscally transparent under the definition of fiscal transparency in Article 10.2.2 unless it is considered a Tax Transparent Entity in certain cases under Article 10.2.4. If the Constituent Entity is not treated as a fiscally transparent Entity under the specific rule in Article 10.2.4, for instance because it has a place of business in the jurisdiction where it was created, then its profits will not be allocated to another Constituent Entity.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p546 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">85.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">If a Constituent </SPAN><NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> is located in a jurisdiction that regards the Constituent Entity as fiscally transparent, this owner could nonetheless be subject to tax on the Constituent Entity’s profits. However, this tax would not be allocated to the Constituent Entity because Article 4.3.2(d) only applies when the Constituent Entity is a Hybrid Entity or a Reverse Hybrid Entity. Under Article 10.2.5, an Entity can only be considered a Hybrid Entity if it is treated as a separate taxable person for income tax purposes in the jurisdiction where it is located. Consequently, the Hybrid Entity definition in Article 10.2.5 does not apply when a Constituent Entity is located in a jurisdiction without a CIT because the Entity will not be treated as a separate taxable person in such a jurisdiction.</P>
<P class="p546 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">86.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">This would lead to a breakdown in the matching principle because the tax of the Constituent Entity- owner will not be included in the same jurisdictional ETR computation as the profit to which it relates. There is also no clear policy justification for only allocating taxes to a Constituent Entity when it is located in a jurisdiction with a CIT.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p525 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">87.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">Accordingly, the Inclusive Framework has agreed to clarify that the Hybrid Entity definition will also apply to an Entity that is not treated as fiscally transparent under Article 10.2.4 and is located in a jurisdiction under Article 10.3.1(b).</SPAN></P>
<P class="p577 ft148">5.5.4. Guidance</P>
<P class="p750 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">88.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">The bold text will be added to the Commentary to 10.2.5:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p768 ft144">169. Article 10.2.5 defines a Hybrid Entity as an Entity that is treated as a separate taxable person for income tax purposes in the jurisdiction where it is located (i.e. a tax resident) but treated as fiscally transparent in the jurisdiction where its owners are located. <SPAN class="ft199">An Entity that is located in a jurisdiction that does not have a Corporate Income Tax will also be treated as a Hybrid Entity if it is treated as fiscally transparent in the jurisdiction where its owners are located and is not treated as a fiscally transparent entity under Article 10.2.4 (for example because</SPAN></P>
<P class="p676 ft153">the Entity has a place of business in the jurisdiction where it was created). The word “owner” refers to both the direct and indirect owner of the Ownership Interests of the Hybrid Entity. <SPAN class="ft119">Similar to other definitions in Article 10.2, the phrase “with respect to its income, expenditure, profit or loss to the extent that it is fiscally transparent in the jurisdiction in which its owner is located” allows that an Entity can be considered a Hybrid Entity only with respect to the owners that treat it as fiscally transparent. The term Hybrid Entity is relevant for purposes of Article 4.3.2(d).</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1268 ft116">TAX CHALLENGES ARISING FROM THE DIGITALISATION OF THE ECONOMY – ADMINISTRATIVE GUIDANCE ON THE GLOBAL <NOBR>ANTI-BASE</NOBR> EROSION MODEL RULES (PILLAR TWO), JUNE 2024 © OECD 2024</P>

<P class="p599 ft148">5.5.5. Examples</P>
<P class="p944 ft149">Example <NOBR>10.2.1-4</NOBR> Extension of Article 10.2.5 to indirect owners</P>
<P class="p625 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft132">Assume A Co wholly owns B Co which in turn wholly owns C Co. A Co is located in Jurisdiction A, B Co in Jurisdiction B and C Co in Jurisdiction C. Jurisdiction A regards both B Co and C Co as fiscally transparent entities. Jurisdiction B’s tax laws do not treat C Co as a fiscally transparent entity. See illustration below.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1269 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft132">C Co is a Hybrid Entity because A Co, the ‘owner’ referred to in Article 10.2.5, is subject to tax on C Co’s profits. Consequently, any taxes paid by A Co with respect to C Co’s profits are allocated to C Co under Article 4.3.2(d).</SPAN></P>
<P class="p565 ft149">Example <NOBR>10.2.1-5</NOBR> Entities located in jurisdictions without a Corporate Income Tax</P>
<P class="p627 ft142"><SPAN class="ft119">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft141">Assume A Co owns B Co. The tax laws of Jurisdiction A treat B Co as fiscally transparent, therefore A Co is subject to tax on B Co’s profits. Jurisdiction B does not have a Corporate Income Tax regime. B Co does not meet the definition of a Tax Transparent Entity under Article 10.2.4 because it has a place of business in Jurisdiction B, where it is created. See illustration below.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1270 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft132">B Co is a Hybrid Entity because it is treated as fiscally transparent in the jurisdiction where its owner is located and is not treated as a fiscally transparent entity under Article 10.2.4.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p649 ft116">TAX CHALLENGES ARISING FROM THE DIGITALISATION OF THE ECONOMY – ADMINISTRATIVE GUIDANCE ON THE GLOBAL <NOBR>ANTI-BASE</NOBR> EROSION MODEL RULES (PILLAR TWO), JUNE 2024 © OECD 2024</P>

<P class="p1271 ft131"><SPAN class="ft131">5.6.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft222">Taxes paid by a Constituent </SPAN><NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> with respect to a Reverse Hybrid Entity’s income</P>
<P class="p1272 ft369"><SPAN class="ft348">5.6.1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft368">Issue 6: Matching of taxes and income where an owner is subject to tax with respect to a Reverse Hybrid Entity’s income</SPAN></P>
<P class="p525 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">89.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">Under this guidance, the tax law of the Reference Entity’s jurisdiction determines whether a Flow- through Entity is treated a Tax Transparent Entity or a Reverse Hybrid Entity. This will generally ensure the profits of a </SPAN><NOBR>Flow-through</NOBR> Entity are allocated consistently with the principles that income should be allocated to the jurisdiction that would be expected to have the primary taxing rights in respect of that income and the matching principle that income and tax with respect to that income should be matched in the same jurisdictional ETR computation.</P>
<P class="p559 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">90.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">However, this rule may not always put the </SPAN><NOBR>Flow-through</NOBR> Entity’s profit and the MNE Group’s tax on that profit in the same jurisdictional ETR computation if the Entity is owned through a chain of Entities. This is because the jurisdictions where the owners are located could take different views on the transparency of an Entity, leading some owner(s) to conclude that an Entity is fiscally transparent and (the) other owner(s) to conclude that it is not fiscally transparent. This inconsistent treatment will lead to a mismatch in the allocation of profits and taxes if an indirect owner views the Entity (and each Entity through which the owner owns its Ownership Interest in the Entity) as fiscally transparent and pays tax on its income, but the Reference Entity views the Entity as fiscally opaque. This is because under this guidance, the Entity will be classified as a Reverse Hybrid Entity (because it is not viewed as fiscally transparent by the Reference Entity), and this will prevent the profits of the Entity from being allocated to the indirect owner that is subject to tax on the Entity’s income. Further, the taxes paid by the indirect owner on this income would not be allocated to the Reverse Hybrid Entity under Article 4.3.2.</P>
<P class="p533 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">91.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">This is illustrated in the following example.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1273 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">92.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">In this example, A Co wholly owns B Co which in turn owns C Co. A Co is located in Jurisdiction A, B Co in Jurisdiction B, and C Co in Jurisdiction C. The table below summarises how each jurisdiction’s tax laws treat the entities.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1274 ft116">TAX CHALLENGES ARISING FROM THE DIGITALISATION OF THE ECONOMY – ADMINISTRATIVE GUIDANCE ON THE GLOBAL <NOBR>ANTI-BASE</NOBR> EROSION MODEL RULES (PILLAR TWO), JUNE 2024 © OECD 2024</P>

<P class="p1276 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">93.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">Because Jurisdiction A’s tax laws consider both B Co and C Co as fiscally transparent, the profits or losses of C Co are included in A Co’s taxable income and subject to tax. These profits or losses are not taxed in either Jurisdiction B, because its tax laws regard C Co as fiscally opaque, or Jurisdiction C, because its tax laws regard C Co as fiscally transparent.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p557 ft128"><SPAN class="ft119">94.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft146">Under Article 10.2.1, C Co is considered a Reverse Hybrid Entity because B Co is the Reference Entity, and the tax laws of Jurisdiction B do not treat C Co as fiscally transparent. This means that the</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1277 ft119">GloBE Income or Loss of C Co is not allocated to another Constituent Entity and is effectively treated as stateless income. The tax paid by A Co with respect to C Co’s income is not allocated to C Co.</P>
<P class="p762 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">95.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft154">This outcome is inconsistent with the policy of matching income and the taxes on that income for</SPAN></P>
<P class="p596 ft119">purposes of the GloBE ETR computations. This could result in double taxation to the extent that <NOBR>Top-up</NOBR> Taxes are paid under an IIR or UTPR in respect of C Co’s profits in addition to the taxes A Co has paid on those profits. Similarly, there are also instances where the direct owners of the Reverse Hybrid Entity are subject to tax on the income of the Reverse Hybrid Entity. Leaving the Covered Tax in the jurisdiction of the direct owners while the profits remaining with the Reverse Hybrid Entity can also lead to double taxation under GloBE.</P>
<P class="p564 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">96.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">Accordingly, the Commentary will be revised to clarify that Covered Taxes paid by a direct or indirect Constituent </SPAN><NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> with respect to the profits of a Reverse Hybrid Entity are allocated to the Reverse Hybrid Entity under Article 4.3.2(d). This will ensure that taxes are appropriately matched with the income that the tax relates to, in line with the matching principles of the GloBE Rules. Article 4.3.2(d) shall apply in the same way to the income of a Reverse Hybrid Entity as it applies to the income of a Hybrid Entity. Accordingly, the allocation of Covered Taxes from a Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> to a Reverse Hybrid Entity will be subject to the passive income limitation in Article 4.3.3.</P>
<P class="p553 ft142"><SPAN class="ft119">97.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft152">For the purposes of computing the ETR under a QDMTT, Paragraphs 118.28 to 118.30 of the Commentary require a QDMTT to exclude from the Adjusted Covered Taxes the Covered Tax expense of a Constituent </SPAN><NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> on income of a Hybrid Entity that is allocable to a Hybrid Entity located in the QDMTT jurisdiction, as well as the Covered Tax expense of a Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> on income of a Reverse Hybrid Entity that is allocable to a Reverse Hybrid Entity created in the QDMTT jurisdiction. For</P>
<P class="p735 ft119">the avoidance of doubt, this requirement does not apply to taxes imposed by a QDMTT jurisdiction itself on a direct or indirect Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner’s</NOBR> share of income of a Reverse Hybrid Entity created in the QDMTT jurisdiction, as such taxes resulted from the QDMTT jurisdiction’s exercise of its primary taxing rights.</P>

<P class="p1261 ft148">5.6.2. Guidance</P>
<P class="p1279 ft314"><SPAN class="ft119">98.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft370">The following additions in bold will be made to the Commentary to Article 4.3.2(d): </SPAN><SPAN class="ft371">Paragraph (d) - Hybrid Entities </SPAN><SPAN class="ft372">and Reverse Hybrid Entities</SPAN></P>
<P class="p617 ft136"><SPAN class="ft119">59.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft373">Paragraph (d) allocates Taxes of Constituent </SPAN><NOBR>Entity-owners</NOBR> arising in connection with the income of Hybrid Entities <SPAN class="ft201">and Reverse Hybrid Entities</SPAN>. If a Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> of a Hybrid Entity <SPAN class="ft201">or Reverse Hybrid Entity </SPAN>is located in a tax jurisdiction that imposes Tax on the owner’s share of the Hybrid Entity<SPAN class="ft214">’s</SPAN><SPAN class="ft201"> or Reverse Hybrid Entity’s </SPAN>income under a fiscal transparency regime (see discussion in Commentary to Article 10.2), the Covered Taxes included in the financial accounts of the Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> should be assigned to the Hybrid Entity <SPAN class="ft201">or Reverse Hybrid Entity</SPAN>. <SPAN class="ft201">In some cases, an indirect Constituent </SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft201">Entity-owner</SPAN></NOBR><SPAN class="ft201"> that is further up the ownership chain than the Reference Entity (i.e. the owner whose tax law determined that</SPAN></P>
<P class="p610 ft210">the <NOBR>Flow-through</NOBR> Entity is treated as a Reverse Hybrid Entity) may be subject to tax on the Reverse Hybrid Entity’s income under a domestic fiscal transparency regime notwithstanding that the Entity is not a Tax Transparent Entity under the GloBE Rules. Similarly, the jurisdiction in which the Reverse Hybrid Entity is created may impose a</P>
<P class="p1280 ft199">Covered Tax on a direct Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> that is located in another jurisdiction in respect of the Reverse Hybrid Entity’s income. In those cases, Taxes of the Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> must be allocated to the Reverse Hybrid Entity in the same manner as if it were a Hybrid Entity. <SPAN class="ft144">The same general process described in paragraph (a) above for allocating Covered Taxes imposed on the Main Entity in respect of a PE can be used to determine the amount of taxes allocated by a Constituent Entity owner to a Hybrid Entity </SPAN>or Reverse Hybrid Entity<SPAN class="ft144">, however any taxes allocated to a Hybrid Entity </SPAN>or Reverse Hybrid Entity <SPAN class="ft144">by a Constituent Entity- owner in respect of Passive Income are subject to limitation under Article 4.3.3, which is discussed further below. If the Constituent </SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft144">Entity-owner</SPAN></NOBR><SPAN class="ft144"> is subject to a withholding tax or net basis taxes on distributions from the Hybrid Entity </SPAN>or Reverse Hybrid Entity<SPAN class="ft144">, such Taxes would also be allocated to the Hybrid Entity </SPAN>or Reverse Hybrid Entity <SPAN class="ft144">pursuant to paragraph (e).</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1281 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">99.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">The bold text will be added to the Commentary to Article 4.3.3:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1282 ft136"><SPAN class="ft119">62.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft147">Article 4.3.3 imposes a limitation on the </SPAN><NOBR>“push-down”</NOBR> of Taxes from a Constituent Entity- owner that are attributable to Passive Income of the subsidiary Constituent Entity. This rule is designed to maintain the integrity of the jurisdictional blending rules in relation to mobile income. In the absence of Article 4.3.3, the rules in Article 4.3.2(c) and (d), which allocate Taxes paid by a Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> under a CFC Tax Regime or in respect of a Hybrid Entity <SPAN class="ft201">or Reverse</SPAN></P>
<P class="p815 ft119"><SPAN class="ft153">Hybrid Entity</SPAN>, would effectively blend the Taxes paid on that mobile income in the Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner’s</NOBR> high tax jurisdiction with other income arising in the <NOBR>Low-Tax</NOBR> Jurisdiction. Without the rule of Article 4.3.3, an MNE Group could shift mobile income from <NOBR>high-tax</NOBR> jurisdictions to <NOBR>Low-Tax</NOBR> Jurisdictions to reduce overall tax liability (including <NOBR>Top-up</NOBR> Tax liability) in the MNE Group.</P>
<P class="p1283 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">100.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft202">The following additions in bold will be made to the Commentary to the definition of a Qualified Domestic Minimum </SPAN><NOBR>Top-up</NOBR> Tax in Article 10.1:</P>
<P class="p1284 ft116">TAX CHALLENGES ARISING FROM THE DIGITALISATION OF THE ECONOMY – ADMINISTRATIVE GUIDANCE ON THE GLOBAL <NOBR>ANTI-BASE</NOBR> EROSION MODEL RULES (PILLAR TWO), JUNE 2024 © OECD 2024</P>

<P class="p761 ft136"><SPAN class="ft119">118.30</SPAN><SPAN class="ft157">For purposes of computing the ETR, a QDMTT shall exclude Covered Tax expense of: (i) a Constituent </SPAN><NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> under a CFC Tax Regime that is allocable to a domestic Constituent Entity under Article 4.3.2(c) of the GloBE Rules; (ii) a Main Entity that is allocable under Article 4.3.2(a) to a Permanent Establishment located in the jurisdiction; (iii) a Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> on income of a Hybrid Entity <SPAN class="ft201">or a Reverse Hybrid Entity </SPAN>that is allocable <SPAN class="ft201">under Article 4.3.2(d) </SPAN>to a Hybrid Entity <SPAN class="ft201">or Reverse Hybrid Entity that is either </SPAN>located in the jurisdiction <SPAN class="ft201">or is included in the scope of the QDMTT because the QDMTT applies to stateless </SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft201">Flow-through</SPAN></NOBR><SPAN class="ft201"> Entities created in the QDMTT jurisdiction </SPAN><SPAN class="ft214">under Article 4.3.2(d)</SPAN>; and (iv) a Constituent <NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> (e.g. net basis taxes), other than a withholding tax imposed by the QDMTT jurisdiction, that is allocable to a distributing Constituent Entity located in the jurisdiction under Article 4.3.2(e). Withholding taxes that are described in Article 4.3.2(e) imposed by the QDMTT jurisdiction itself on distributions from a Constituent Entity located in the QDMTT jurisdiction are allocated to the distributing Constituent Entity under the QDMTT. <SPAN class="ft201">Similarly, Covered Taxes accrued in the financial accounts of a Constituent </SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft201">Entity-owner</SPAN></NOBR><SPAN class="ft201"> of a Hybrid Entity or Reverse Hybrid Entity are included in the Adjusted Covered Taxes of the Hybrid Entity or Reverse Hybrid Entity where the taxes (a) are allocated to the Hybrid Entity or Reverse Hybrid Entity under Article 4.3.2(d), (b) are imposed by the jurisdiction of the Hybrid Entity or Reverse Hybrid Entity and (c) relate to the income of the Hybrid Entity or Reverse Hybrid Entity. This could include for example taxes in respect of immovable property located in the QDMTT jurisdiction.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1285 ft148"><SPAN class="ft348">5.6.3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft349">Examples</SPAN></P>
<P class="p656 ft149">Example <NOBR>10.2.1-6</NOBR></P>
<P class="p627 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft132">Assume A Co owns B Co and B Co owns C Co. A Co is not a </SPAN><NOBR>Flow-through</NOBR> Entity. The tax law of the jurisdiction in which A Co is located, Jurisdiction A, treats A Co as fiscally opaque and B Co as fiscally transparent and C Co as fiscally transparent. B Co is not a <NOBR>Flow-through</NOBR> Entity. The tax law of the jurisdiction in which B Co is created, Jurisdiction B, does not treat C Co as fiscally transparent. The tax law of the jurisdiction in which C Co is created treats C Co as fiscally transparent. Assume B Co’s profit is 100 and C Co’s profit is 200. See illustration below.</P>
<P class="p1286 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft132">B Co is the Reference Entity because it is the closest Constituent </SPAN><NOBR>Entity-owner</NOBR> to C Co that is not a <NOBR>Flow-through</NOBR> Entity. Because Jurisdiction B’s tax laws do not treat C Co as fiscally transparent, C Co’s income will not be subject to tax in Jurisdiction B. C Co would consequently be treated as a Reverse Hybrid Entity.</P>

<P class="p1290 ft341"><SPAN class="ft340">6.</SPAN> Treatment of Securitisation Vehicles</P>
<P class="p1291 ft131">6.1. Securitisation Vehicles</P>
<P class="p594 ft148">6.1.1. Introduction</P>
<P class="p710 ft119"><SPAN class="ft128">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft374">Securitisation is a financing technique that enables a creditor (the “originator”) – typically a credit institution or a corporation – to refinance a set of loans, exposures or receivables, such as residential loans, auto loans or leases, consumer loans, credit cards or trade receivables, by transforming them into tradable securities.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p555 ft119"><SPAN class="ft128">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft138">The originator pools and repackages a portfolio of its assets and typically organises them into different risk categories for different investors, thus giving investors access to investments in assets to which they normally would not have direct access and enabling the originator to raise finance at a lower cost. Returns to investors are generated from the cash flows of the assets.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p553 ft144"><SPAN class="ft128">3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft143">The technique requires the repackaged portfolio of assets to be isolated from the credit risk of the originator. This is accomplished by using special purpose vehicles (SPVs) to hold the assets (or assets deriving their value from them) and issue the debt secured on them, thus making the wider creditworthiness of the originator irrelevant to the credit risk assumed by the holders of the SPV’s debt instruments. Such SPVs are often referred to as “bankruptcy remote” because of this isolation of the assets.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p606 ft148">6.1.2. Overview</P>
<P class="p569 ft119"><SPAN class="ft128">4.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft138">In a classical securitisation transaction, assets producing the relevant revenue streams – (for example loans, mortgages, bonds, leases, or contracts corresponding to the performance of such assets or exposures) will be transferred by the originator to an SPV (or multiple SPVs). These SPVs could take the form of a company or a trust or a similar arrangement depending on the structure concerned.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p555 ft119"><SPAN class="ft128">5.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft138">Where the SPV is a company, the SPV will typically be owned by an unconnected third party which does not consolidate the SPV. Where it is a trust or similar arrangement, the originator may hold Ownership Interests in the SPV, or it may not hold such Ownership Interests which could instead be held by an unconnected third party. In the case of a securitisation transaction with multiple SPVs, one SPV may hold all of the Ownership Interests of another SPV (e.g. all of the ordinary shares of a company) but the Ownership Interests in the upper tier SPV may be owned by an unconnected third party. This facilitates the bankruptcy remoteness of the SPV from the originator, by ensuring it will not be subject to secondary liabilities and isolates the risk of the asset pool (which is further described below) from the wider credit risk associated with the originator.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1292 ft116">TAX CHALLENGES ARISING FROM THE DIGITALISATION OF THE ECONOMY – ADMINISTRATIVE GUIDANCE ON THE GLOBAL <NOBR>ANTI-BASE</NOBR> EROSION MODEL RULES (PILLAR TWO), JUNE 2024 © OECD 2024</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2">
<P class="p11 ft2">247</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="page_248">


<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p11 ft2">Prop. 2025/26:22</P>
<P class="p485 ft2">Bilaga 1</P>
<P class="p521 ft24"><SPAN class="ft153">140</SPAN><SPAN class="ft118">|</SPAN></P>
<P class="p522 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">6.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft132">The SPV may be consolidated into the same group as the originator, and consequently be a Constituent Entity in the originator’s Group under the GloBE Rules. This could be due to the originator’s Ownership Interests in the SPV or due to a servicing agreement or other arrangement that the originator enters into with the SPV, under which the originator takes responsibility for the </SPAN><NOBR>day-to-day</NOBR> management of the asset pool. This (together with the cash extraction mechanism below) can lead to it being treated as having control under some financial accounting standards. Even within the same accounting standard, the consolidation requirements can be sensitive to the precise details and structuring of the arrangement, like the terms of the servicing agreement or other arrangement. It is often not clear cut and there are many cases where the question of whether to consolidate an SPV into its originators group is difficult and nuanced (and where different auditors can take different views of the same arrangements). The outcome can have significant implications under the GloBE Rules, because the SPV would be treated as a Constituent Entity of the originator’s Group in cases where it is consolidated.</P>
<P class="p536 ft136"><SPAN class="ft119">7.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft133">The SPV will issue debt instruments normally via the bond markets. The proceeds of the debt instruments issued are used to finance the acquisition of the asset pool. The payment stream on the assets is then used to service the debt instruments. In a synthetic securitisation, the underlying asset pool is not transferred to an SPV. Instead, the SPV becomes party to a derivative contract or guarantee under which it assumes the risk of the performance of the underlying asset pool, while itself also owning highly secure assets such as government debt. The combination of returns from the highly secure assets and additional</SPAN></P>
<P class="p537 ft119">payments received from the originator group in consideration of the SPV becoming party to the derivative contract or guarantee in relation to the underlying asset pool put the SPV – and hence its creditors in the same economic position as if the SPV had itself owned the underlying asset pool.</P>
<P class="p546 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">8.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft132">The originator (or another Constituent Entity in the same MNE Group as the originator) will often also hold some of the debt instruments issued by the SPV (which commonly rank junior to the debt issued to </SPAN><NOBR>third-party</NOBR> creditors). This enables the SPV to hold more collateral in the form of the underlying asset pool than the principal on the debt instruments issued to third parties, thus replicating the economic effect of typical commercial transactions where <NOBR>third-party</NOBR> lenders will generally require security over underlying assets with a greater value than the amount they are lending. This reduces the risk of the <NOBR>third-party</NOBR> lenders because any losses would first fall on the originator. This overcollateralization and the bankruptcy remoteness described above enables <NOBR>third-party</NOBR> loan notes to be issued at a lower cost than if the originator had borrowed directly.</P>
<P class="p536 ft136"><SPAN class="ft119">9.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft133">The SPV generally has an asset pool yielding more income than it is expected to need to meet its liabilities. This incorporates a margin of error if some of the assets do not produce as much income as expected. It also means the transferred asset pool will often yield a greater amount than is necessary to service and repay the SPV’s debt instruments. The SPV is only designed to make a negligible profit, at most, on the difference between the payment stream it receives from the underlying asset pool and its costs servicing the debt instruments so the structure will typically include a mechanism to return any excess</SPAN></P>
<P class="p537 ft119">cash from the SPV to the originator or another Constituent Entity in the same MNE Group as the originator (“cash extraction mechanism”). The precise form of the cash extraction mechanism varies depending on the structure, but payments are commonly made on a monthly or quarterly basis so surplus cash is typically not retained in the SPV for a significant period of time.</P>
<P class="p572 ft149">Hedging arrangements</P>
<P class="p576 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">10.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">As noted above, SPVs are generally structured so they only make a negligible profit (at most) over the life of the transaction, after taking into account the impact of the cash extraction mechanism. This is because the cash extraction mechanism will require surplus cash to be paid out to the originator (or another Constituent Entity in the same MNE Group as the originator).</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1293 ft116">TAX CHALLENGES ARISING FROM THE DIGITALISATION OF THE ECONOMY – ADMINISTRATIVE GUIDANCE ON THE GLOBAL <NOBR>ANTI-BASE</NOBR> EROSION MODEL RULES (PILLAR TWO), JUNE 2024 © OECD 2024</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2">
<P class="p11 ft2">248</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="page_249">


<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p513 ft2">Prop. 2025/26:22</P>
<P class="p514 ft2">Bilaga 1</P>
<P class="p1145 ft112"><SPAN class="ft24">| </SPAN>141</P>
<P class="p539 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">11.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">Despite this, SPVs can recognise significant profits or losses in their Financial Accounting Net Income or Loss in a given Fiscal Year. This can arise through hedging arrangements, which SPVs use to hedge risks that could lead to the payment stream from the asset pool becoming insufficient to meet the SPV’s liabilities under the debt instruments. These commonly include currency hedges where the loan notes were issued in a different currency than the currency of the asset pool or interest rate swaps where the SPV is exposed to interest rate risk (for example if the assets carry a fixed rate of interest but debt instruments carry a variable rate of interest).</SPAN></P>
<P class="p564 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">12.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">Where the SPV is unable to, or does not, adopt hedge accounting, these hedging instruments can be subject to fair value accounting and changes in their fair value will lead to profits or losses being recognised in the income statement. This can create a mismatch if the corresponding profit or loss on the hedged asset or liability is not also subject to fair value accounting.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p556 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">13.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">Many SPVs do not as a rule recognise deferred tax. This can be because the SPV is exempt from Corporate Income Tax or because the hedged profits and losses are excluded from the tax base and the SPV is only subject to Corporate Income Tax on the negligible profit it has made in the Fiscal Year. Where deferred tax is not recognised, there will not be an amount in the Adjusted Covered Taxes to offset the impact of the GloBE Income or Loss attributable to the hedge. This could lead to a </SPAN><NOBR>top-up</NOBR> tax in relation to the Fiscal Years where fair value profits arise from the hedge, even though the SPV will not recognise more than a negligible profit from the overall transaction.</P>
<P class="p562 ft148">6.1.3. Issues to be considered</P>
<P class="p944 ft149">Impact of imposing a <NOBR>top-up</NOBR> tax liability on the SPV</P>
<P class="p564 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">14.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">Securitisation transactions are designed to achieve objectives such as lowering the originator’s cost of borrowing or reducing its liquidity risks by transferring assets to a bankruptcy remote entity that is removed from the wider risks of the originator and is thus able to achieve a better credit rating. This could be significantly undermined if the SPV became liable to </SPAN><NOBR>top-up</NOBR> tax charges under the GloBE Rules because the exposure to a potential <NOBR>top-up</NOBR> tax charge elsewhere in the group would mean the SPV is no longer actually insulated from the originator Group. This could impact the solvency of the SPV and lead credit rating agencies to downgrade its credit rating (even before any tax liability materialises), which could affect the viability of many securitisation transactions.</P>
<P class="p944 ft149">Treatment of profits or losses arising in a securitisation vehicle</P>
<P class="p566 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">15.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">The Model Rules have generally been designed to ensure that the GloBE Rules do not impose </SPAN><NOBR>top-up</NOBR> taxes when the MNE Group has not made an economic profit in the jurisdiction or because income has been taxed in a different period than the period in which the income is recognised in under the GloBE Rules.</P>
<P class="p553 ft136"><SPAN class="ft119">16.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft147">As noted above, SPVs used in securitisation transactions will be structured so that any surplus cash recognised by a SPV will be paid to the originator and so the SPV cannot make more than a negligible profit from the arrangement (after taking into account the cash extraction mechanism). As the SPV will, at most, make a negligible economic profit over the life of the arrangement, the SPV would not be expected to give rise to significant </SPAN><NOBR>top-up</NOBR> taxes under the GloBE Rules even if that negligible profit was untaxed.</P>
<P class="p729 ft136"><SPAN class="ft119">17.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft147">However, fair value movements, for example in relation to hedging arrangements, can give rise to significant profits or losses in a given Fiscal Year. Furthermore, the mechanisms in the Model Rules to deal with this volatility in the profit and loss may not always work effectively for SPVs because deferred tax is not usually recognised. Consequently, there will not be a corresponding amount of Adjusted Covered Taxes to offset the impact of these amounts of GloBE Income or GloBE Loss. This could lead to </SPAN><NOBR>top-up</NOBR> taxes being payable that are not commensurate with the economic profit the SPV has made.</P>
<P class="p601 ft116">TAX CHALLENGES ARISING FROM THE DIGITALISATION OF THE ECONOMY – ADMINISTRATIVE GUIDANCE ON THE GLOBAL <NOBR>ANTI-BASE</NOBR> EROSION MODEL RULES (PILLAR TWO), JUNE 2024 © OECD 2024</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2">
<P class="p11 ft2">249</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="page_250">


<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p11 ft2">Prop. 2025/26:22</P>
<P class="p485 ft2">Bilaga 1</P>
<P class="p521 ft24"><SPAN class="ft153">142</SPAN><SPAN class="ft118">|</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1261 ft148">6.1.4. Guidance</P>
<P class="p537 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">18.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">The Inclusive Framework agrees that jurisdictions adopting QDMTTs are not required to impose </SPAN><NOBR>top-up</NOBR> tax liabilities on SPVs used in securitisation transactions. The Commentary will consequently be revised to clarify that a QDMTT liability in respect of a Securitisation Entity should generally be imposed on other Constituent Entities located in the jurisdiction. The Commentary will also clarify that a QDMTT may exclude a Securitisation Entity from its scope (such that the Securitisation Entity is not treated as a Constituent Entity for the purposes of that QDMTT).</P>
<P class="p546 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">19.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">The Inclusive Framework also agrees that QDMTTs that impose the </SPAN><NOBR>top-up</NOBR> tax liability computed for a Securitisation Entity on other Constituent Entities located in the jurisdiction or that exclude Securitisation Entities from the scope of the tax would both still meet the Consistency Standard for the purposes of the QDMTT Safe Harbour. Revisions will consequently be made to the Commentary to add these to the <NOBR>Switch-off</NOBR> Rule.</P>
<P class="p1211 ft136"><SPAN class="ft119">20.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft147">The Commentary already provides that Article 2.4.1 does not prescribe how the UTPR </SPAN><NOBR>Top-up</NOBR> Tax Amount is allocated among the Constituent Entities that are located in the UTPR jurisdiction. Therefore, jurisdictions may exclude Securitisation Entities from liability to <NOBR>top-up</NOBR> taxes under the UTPR. A jurisdiction that excludes Securitisation Entities from liability to <NOBR>top-up</NOBR> taxes under the UTPR would not be in a position to impose any additional cash tax expense in the scenario where the Securitisation Entity is the only Constituent Entity located in the jurisdiction. In the unlikely scenario where the UTPR jurisdiction would be allocated UTPR <NOBR>Top-up</NOBR> Tax in a year when a Securitisation Entity is the only Constituent Entity located in the jurisdiction, Article 2.6.3 provides that this jurisdiction would be excluded from the allocation mechanism provided under Article 2.6.1 in subsequent Fiscal Years if the <NOBR>top-up</NOBR> tax remains uncollected.</P>
<P class="p1294 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">21.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">As a Securitisation Entity would not be expected to be a Parent Entity within a MNE Group, it would not in practice be liable to a </SPAN><NOBR>top-up</NOBR> tax charge under the IIR and so no changes to the Commentary are necessary.</P>
<P class="p525 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">22.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">The Inclusive Framework also recognises Securitisation Entities can have significant accounting profits or losses in a given Fiscal Year, even in circumstances where negligible economic profit or loss is realised over the life of the transaction. It will in a timely manner consider issuing further Administrative Guidance to ensure that the use of securitisation transactions (and arrangements of the kind entered into by SPVs that give rise to fair value movements) do not result in MNE Groups paying </SPAN><NOBR>top-up</NOBR> taxes that are not commensurate with the economic profit that the SPV has made from the activities. This will include considering whether a Securitisation Entity should be treated as being deconsolidated from the MNE Group for the purposes of the GloBE Rules and whether these issues could be addressed by making an adjusted realisation basis election available in relation to the profits of SPVs. Further consideration will also be given to the treatment of any distributions received by the originator or any Constituent Entities in the MNE Group from the SPV.</P>
<P class="p851 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">23.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft145">The following paragraph will be inserted into the Commentary to the definition of Qualified Domestic Minimum </SPAN><NOBR>Top-up</NOBR> Tax in Article 10.1</P>
<P class="p797 ft153">Securitisation Entity</P>
<P class="p667 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">118.40.10</SPAN><SPAN class="ft362">Securitisation Entities are designed to be bankruptcy remote from the originator and the other Constituent Entities of the MNE Group. A jurisdiction may therefore allocate the liability for any QDMTT </SPAN><NOBR>top-up</NOBR> tax to another Constituent Entity (if any) that is located in the jurisdiction. A QDMTT may also include provisions that ensure the <NOBR>top-up</NOBR> tax cannot be imposed on a Securitisation Entity. A QDMTT may also exclude a Securitisation Entity from its scope (i.e. the Securitisation Entity could be excluded from the Effective Tax Rate calculation for the jurisdiction). In this case, the income of such Securitisation Entities would remain within the scope of the GloBE Rules.</P>

<P class="p807 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">24.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft154">The following paragraphs will be added to the Commentary to Article 10.1:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p762 ft153">Securitisation Entity</P>
<P class="p626 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">148.1</SPAN><SPAN class="ft164">Special purpose entities used in securitisation transactions (securitisation entities) are structured so they only make, at most, a negligible profit over the life of the transaction. This is because the arrangements between the securitisation entity and the originator of the assets will typically include a cash extraction mechanism that requires surplus cash to be paid out to the originator (or another Constituent Entity in the same MNE Group as the originator).</SPAN></P>
<P class="p747 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">148.2</SPAN><SPAN class="ft375">A “Securitisation Entity” means an Entity which is a participant in a Securitisation Arrangement, and which satisfies all of the following conditions:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1296 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">a.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft155">the Entity only carries out activities that facilitate one or more Securitisation Arrangements</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1297 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">b.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft155">it grants security over its assets in favour of its creditors (or the creditors of another Securitisation Entity)</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1297 ft119"><SPAN class="ft128">c.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft156">it pays out all cash received from its assets to its creditors (or the creditors of another Securitisation Entity) on an annual or more frequent basis, other than:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1298 ft119"><SPAN class="ft128">i.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft155">cash retained to meet an amount of profit required by the documentation of the arrangement, for eventual distribution to equity holders (or equivalent); or</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1299 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">ii.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft155">cash reasonably required under the terms of the arrangement for either (or both) of the following purposes:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1300 ft119"><SPAN class="ft128">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft155">to make provision for future payments which are required, or will likely be required, to be made by the Entity under the terms of the arrangement; or</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1301 ft119"><SPAN class="ft128">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft155">to maintain or enhance the creditworthiness of the Entity</SPAN></P>
<P class="p808 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">148.3</SPAN><SPAN class="ft164">An Entity shall not be treated as a Securitisation Entity unless any profit referred to in paragraph 148.2(c)(i) above for a given Fiscal Year is negligible relative to the revenues of the Entity.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1302 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">148.4</SPAN><SPAN class="ft204">A Securitisation Arrangement means an arrangement which satisfies the following conditions:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1303 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">a.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft155">It is implemented for the purpose of pooling and repackaging a portfolio of assets (or exposures to assets) for investors that are not Constituent Entities of the MNE Group in a manner that legally segregates one or more identified pools of assets and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1304 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">b.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft155">It seeks through contractual agreements to limit the exposure of those investors to the risk of insolvency of an Entity holding the legally segregated assets by controlling the ability of identified creditors of that Entity (or of another Entity in the arrangement) to make claims against it through legally binding documentation entered into by those creditors.</SPAN></P>

<P class="p748 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">(a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft130">A QDMTT jurisdiction decides not to impose a QDMTT on </SPAN><NOBR>Flow-through</NOBR> Entities created in its jurisdiction.</P>
<P class="p1305 ft314"><SPAN class="ft119">(b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft376">A QDMTT jurisdiction decides not to impose a QDMTT on Investment Entities subject to Articles 7.4, 7.5, and 7.6 of the GloBE Rules.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1141 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">(c)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft362">A QDMTT jurisdiction decides to adopt Article 9.3 in a QDMTT legislation with no limitation (i.e., option three of paragraph 118.51 of the QDMTT Commentary).</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1306 ft119"><SPAN class="ft119">(d)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft130">A QDMTT jurisdiction includes members of a JV Group (which includes Joint Ventures) within the scope of the QDMTT but imposes the liability on Constituent Entities of the main group instead of directly on the members of the JV Group as permitted under paragraph 118.11 of the QDMTT Commentary.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p814 ft153"><SPAN class="ft153">(e)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft377">A QDMTT jurisdiction decides not to impose a QDMTT on Securitisation Entities.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1307 ft348">Example 10 Securitisation Entities</P>
<P class="p1308 ft201"><SPAN class="ft153">49.1</SPAN><SPAN class="ft378">A jurisdiction may decide not to impose a QDMTT on Securitisation Entities. This could be because Securitisation Entities are not included within the scope of the QDMTT. Alternatively, Securitisation Entities could be included within the scope of the QDMTT, but the QDMTT could include provisions that ensure any </SPAN><NOBR>top-up</NOBR> tax liabilities cannot be imposed on a Securitisation Entity. In either case, the Consistency Standard will still be met notwithstanding the QDMTT is not imposed on these Securitisation Entities. The MNE Group will apply the <NOBR>Switch-off</NOBR> Rule with respect to the jurisdiction where the Securitisation Entity is located. However, where the jurisdiction includes Securitisation Entities within the scope of its QDMTT, but includes provisions to impose any <NOBR>top-up</NOBR> tax liability in respect of the income of a Securitisation Entity on another CE of the MNE Group that is not a Securitisation Entity, or on the Securitisation Entity itself if the <NOBR>top-up</NOBR> tax liability cannot be otherwise collected, the MNE group will not apply the <NOBR>Switch-off</NOBR> Rule with respect to the jurisdiction where the Securitisation Entity is located (i.e. the MNE Group would be allowed to apply the QDMTT Safe Harbour for the QDMTT jurisdiction).</P>

<P class="p11 ft57">Sammanfattning av promemorian Ytterligare kompletteringar till bestämmelserna om tilläggsskatt för företag i stora koncerner</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_1_2">
<P class="p11 ft4">Prop. 2025/26:22 Bilaga 2</P>

<DIV id="id_2">
<P class="p257 ft2">I denna promemoria lämnas förslag på ytterligare kompletteringar till bestämmelserna om tilläggsskatt för företag i stora koncerner, lagen (2023:875) om tilläggsskatt. Genom lagen om tilläggsskatt genomfördes direktivet om säkerställande av en global minimiskattenivå för multinationella koncerner och storskaliga nationella koncerner i unionen (minimibeskattningsdirektivet). Syftet med direktivet är att genomföra de modellregler avseende en global minimibeskattning som arbetats fram inom ramen för OECD/G20:s Inclusive Framework on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS), kallat det inkluderande ramverket (IF). Modellreglerna kompletteras av förklaringar och exempel i Tax Challenges Arising from the Digitalisation of the Economy – Commentary to the Global <NOBR>Anti-Base</NOBR> Erosion Model Rules (Pillar Two), även kallad kommentaren, som godkänts av IF. Kommentaren syftar till att klargöra tolkning och tillämpning av reglerna. Vidare har IF antagit administrativa riktlinjer dvs. Tax Challenges Arising from the Digitalisation of the Economy – Administrative Guidance on the Global <NOBR>Anti-Base</NOBR> Erosion Model Rules (Pillar Two) med kompletteringar till kommentaren som syftar till att ytterligare klargöra tolkning och tillämpning av reglerna.</P>
<P class="p1310 ft2">Den 24 maj 2024 antog IF ytterligare sådana administrativa riktlinjer som publicerades i juni 2024, nedan administrativa riktlinjer från juni 2024<SPAN class="ft14">1</SPAN>. I den utsträckning det är fråga om förtydliganden och exempel så omfattas riktlinjerna redan av de bestämmelser som finns i lagen om tilläggsskatt. Lagen om tilläggsskatt för företag i stora koncerner behöver dock kompletteras med ytterligare eller ändrade bestämmelser. Detta gäller till den del som det är nödvändigt med ny lagstiftning med anledning av dessa administrativa riktlinjer.</P>
<P class="p1311 ft6">Lagändringarna föreslås träda i kraft den 1 januari 2026. Det lämnas dock ett förslag om att det ska införas en möjlighet för den rapporterande enheten att begära att samtliga eller vissa av bestämmelserna ska tillämpas första gången för beskattningsår som börjar närmast efter den 31 december 2023 eller, i fråga om svenska handelsbolag, räkenskapsår som börjar närmast efter den 31 december 2023.</P>

<P class="p1347 ft3">23 a §</P>
<P class="p1348 ft30">Med värdet beträffande tilläggsskatt avses det värde som tillgångar, skulder, intäkter eller kostnader tas upp till vid beräkning av det justerade resultatet.</P>
<P class="p1349 ft17">3 kap.</P>
<P class="p1350 ft3">27 a §</P>
<P class="p1351 ft3">Om utländsk skatt enligt lokala regler avräknas genom att hela den utländska skatten läggs samman och avräknas mot en moderenhets lokala skatt på inkomst som härrör från källa i en annan stat enligt 27 c § ska kostnaden för medräknade skatter som avser utdelning i moderenhetens räken- skaper fördelas enligt bestäm- melserna i 27 <NOBR>b–27</NOBR> d §§. Om flera lokala skatter tas ut på olika</P>
<P class="p1352 ft15">beskattningsunderlag ska fördelningen göras för varje sådan lokal skatt för sig.</P>
<P class="p1353 ft3">Om utländsk skatt enligt lokala regler avräknas separat inom olika inkomstkategorier ska fördelningen enligt 27 <NOBR>b–27</NOBR> d §§ göras för varje sådan kategori för sig. Inkomst som härrör från källa i den stat där moderenheten hör hemma ska då hänföras till den kategori dit utländsk skatt på sådan inkomst hör.</P>
<P class="p1354 ft3">27 b §</P>
<P class="p1355 ft15">Kostnaden för medräknade skatter ska fördelas från moder- enheten till dess fasta driftställen och enheter. Det belopp som ska fördelas ska motsvaras av medräknade skatter att fördela</P>

<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p115 ft30">enligt 27 c § multiplicerat med kvoten av det fasta driftställets eller enhetens fördelningsbelopp och</P>
<P class="p27 ft5">summan av samtliga fördelningsbelopp.</P>
<P class="p265 ft3">27 c §</P>
<P class="p110 ft3">Med <SPAN class="ft29">medräknade skatter att fördela</SPAN> avses en huvudenhets eller moderenhets totala aktuella skattekostnad enligt lokala regler minskat med</P>
<P class="p129 ft15"><SPAN class="ft3">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft38">ett belopp som motsvarar lokal skatt på inkomst som inte härrör från källa i en annan stat,</SPAN></P>
<P class="p108 ft3"><SPAN class="ft3">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft31">skatt som ska fördelas enligt 7 kap. 63 </SPAN><NOBR>a–63</NOBR> e §§, och</P>
<P class="p109 ft16"><SPAN class="ft3">3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft40">ett belopp som motsvarar lokal skatt som avser andra inkomst- kategorier än den kategori som fördelningen av skatten avser, om fördelning ska ske på det sätt som anges i 27 a § andra stycket.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p28 ft3">Om skattesatsen för en moderenhet är progressiv ska beloppet i första stycket 1 beräknas genom att inkomsten hänförs till de tillämpliga skattesatserna i proportion till den lokala inkomstens andel av hela inkomsten.</P>
<P class="p1356 ft15">Med <SPAN class="ft48">inkomst som härrör från källa i en annan stat</SPAN> avses</P>
<P class="p28 ft3">– inkomst som enligt lokala regler om avräkning av utländsk skatt härrör från källa i en annan stat, och</P>
<P class="p28 ft15">– annan inkomst, om inkomsten ingår i det justerade resultatet för ett fast driftställe, ett kontrollerat utländskt företag, en hybridenhet eller en omvänd hybridenhet som hör hemma i en annan stat.</P>
<P class="p351 ft3">27 d §</P>
<P class="p28 ft15">Fördelningsbeloppet för ett fast driftställe beräknas genom att huvudenhetens inkomst från det fasta driftstället multipliceras med tillämplig skattesats i den stat där huvudenheten hör hemma. Det</P>

<P class="p1357 ft15">beräknade beloppet minskas sedan med avräkningsbar utländsk skatt på inkomsten, dock lägst till noll.</P>
<P class="p1358 ft3">Fördelningsbeloppet för en huvudenhet eller moderenhet beräknas genom att annan inkomst som härrör från källa i en annan stat än utdelning eller inkomst från fast driftställe, multipliceras med tillämplig skattesats i den stat där huvudenheten hör hemma. Det beräknade beloppet minskas sedan med avräkningsbar utländsk skatt på inkomsten, dock lägst till noll. Om olika skattesatser gäller för inkomsterna, ska summan av inkomsterna i varje inkomstslag multipliceras med tillämplig skattesats och minskas med avräkningsbar utländsk skatt för varje inkomstslag.</P>
<P class="p1359 ft3">Fördelningsbeloppet för en enhet som lämnar utdelning beräknas genom att lämnad utdelning multipliceras med tillämplig skattesats i den stat där moderenheten hör hemma. Det beräknade beloppet minskas sedan med avräkningsbar utländsk skatt på inkomsten, dock lägst till noll.</P>
<P class="p1360 ft3">30 a §</P>
<P class="p1361 ft3">Om värdet beträffande tilläggs- skatt för en tillgång, skuld, intäkt eller kostnad skiljer sig åt från det värde samma post har enligt räkenskaperna ska uppskjuten skatt beräknas utifrån värdet beträffande tilläggsskatt i stället för värdet enligt räkenskaperna.</P>

<P class="p108 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft44">utländsk skatt får avräknas mot enhetens skatt på den utländska inkomsten först efter kvittning enligt 1,</SPAN></P>
<P class="p26 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft44">utländsk skatt inte får avräknas senare år, och</SPAN></P>
<P class="p28 ft6"><SPAN class="ft2">4.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft42">den inhemska förlust som helt eller delvis har kvittats enligt 1 ett tidigare år beaktas vid omklassificering av inhemsk inkomst till utländsk.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p28 ft2">Skattefordran ska uppgå till den inhemska förlusten som kvittas enligt första stycket 1 multiplicerad med det lägsta av den nationella skattesatsen och minimiskattesatsen.</P>
<P class="p109 ft43">Om den nationella skattesatsen överstiger minimiskattesatsen, ska den fiktiva uppskjutna skattefordran räknas om genom att beloppet enligt andra stycket multipliceras med minimiskattesatsen och divideras med den tillämpliga nationella skattesatsen. Om den nationella skattesatsen därefter ändras, ska kvarstående belopp räknas om enligt den nya skattesatsen.</P>

<P class="p108 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft44">utländsk skatt får avräknas mot enhetens skatt på den utländska inkomsten först efter kvittning enligt 1, och</SPAN></P>
<P class="p28 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft44">belopp som inte avräknats ett tidigare år får avräknas senare år mot skatt på den inhemska inkomst som ingår i beräkningen av enhetens justerade resultat.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p26 ft2">Den särskilda uppskjutna skattefordran ska uppgå till det lägsta av</P>
<P class="p108 ft6"><SPAN class="ft2">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft42">det högsta tillåtna avräkningsbeloppet som enligt nationella regler får beaktas ett senare år, och</SPAN></P>
<P class="p108 ft4"><SPAN class="ft2">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft76">moderenhetens inhemska förlust för beskattningsåret enligt nationella regler multiplicerad med den nationella skattesatsen.</SPAN></P>

<P class="p348 ft6">Om den nationella skattesatsen överstiger minimiskattesatsen, ska den särskilda uppskjutna skattefordran räknas om genom att beloppet enligt andra stycket multipliceras med minimiskattesatsen och divideras med den tillämpliga nationella skattesatsen. Om den nationella skattesatsen därefter ändras, ska kvarstående belopp räknas om enligt den nya skattesatsen.</P>
<P class="p1364 ft2">36 §</P>
<P class="p349 ft6">Bestämmelsen i 35 § första stycket gäller inte om den uppskjutna skatteskulden avser</P>
<P class="p53 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft32">värdeminskningsavdrag avseende materiella tillgångar,</SPAN></P>
<P class="p54 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft32">kostnader för licenser eller liknande tillgångar som gäller i förhållande till en offentlig förvaltning och ger rätt att använda fast egendom eller nyttja en naturresurs, om nyttjandet medför betydande investeringar i materiella tillgångar,</SPAN></P>
<P class="p53 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft32">kostnader för forskning och utveckling,</SPAN></P>
<P class="p53 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">4.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft32">kostnader för avveckling och sanering,</SPAN></P>
<P class="p53 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">5.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft32">orealiserade nettovinster vid redovisning till verkligt värde,</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1325 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">6.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft32">orealiserade nettovinster som beror på fluktuationer i utländsk valuta,</SPAN></P>
<P class="p141 ft6"><SPAN class="ft2">7.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft45">försäkringsreserver och förutbetalda anskaffningskostnader för försäkringsavtal,</SPAN></P>
<P class="p54 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">8.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft32">vinster från försäljning av materiella anläggningstillgångar i samma stat som koncernenheten hör hemma i, om vinsterna återinvesteras i materiella anläggningstillgångar i samma stat, eller</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1365 ft6"><SPAN class="ft2">9.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft45">ytterligare belopp som lagts till i redovisningen som en följd av en förändring av redovisningsprinciperna för de poster som avses i </SPAN><NOBR>1–8.</NOBR></P>
<P class="p132 ft3">Om en leasegivare behandlar ett leasingavtal avseende materiella tillgångar som en fordran i räkenskaperna men som en materiell tillgång vid inkomst- beskattningen, ska en uppskjuten skatteskuld som är hänförlig till värdeminskningsavdrag avseende tillgången omfattas av första stycket 1.</P>
<P class="p1366 ft17">4 kap.</P>
<P class="p1367 ft48">Alternativregel för uppskjuten skatt som ska fördelas till en koncernenhet</P>
<P class="p1368 ft3">16 a §</P>
<P class="p1369 ft3">En rapporterande enhet kan välja att inte tillämpa 3 kap. 27 §, 7 kap. 25 a, 63 <NOBR>f–63</NOBR> i och 64 a– 64 d §§ om fördelning av upp- skjuten skatt för en stat. Om ett sådant val görs ska den uppskjutna skatten inte ingå i den justerade skattekostnaden för vare sig</P>

</DIV>
</DIV>

<P class="p96 ft2">En minoritetsägd koncernenhet som är en svensk koncernenhet är skattskyldig för hela det tilläggsskattebelopp som beräknats och fördelats på enheten enligt 7 kap. 41 §.</P>
<P class="p96 ft2">Ett fast driftställe som är statslöst enligt 1 kap. 15 § är skattskyldigt för hela det tilläggsskattebelopp som beräknats för enheten enligt 3 kap. 42 §, under förutsättning att</P>
<P class="p399 ft6"><SPAN class="ft2">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft42">platsen för affärsverksamhet från vilken verksamhet bedrivs finns i Sverige, eller</SPAN></P>
<P class="p96 ft6"><SPAN class="ft2">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft42">verksamheten, om den inte bedrivs från någon viss plats, är att likställa med affärsverksamhet som bedrivs av en huvudenhet på en plats</SPAN></P>
<P class="p11 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">i</SPAN><SPAN class="ft32">Sverige.</SPAN></P>

<DIV id="id_1_2">
<P class="p1373 ft2">2 a §<SPAN class="ft14">6</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1374 ft6">En svensk koncernenhet är skattskyldig för hela det tilläggsskattebelopp som beräknats och fördelats på ett samriskföretag och ett dotterföretag till ett samriskföretag enligt 7 kap. 45 §, om företaget</P>
<P class="p1375 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft32">hör hemma i Sverige, och</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1375 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft32">tillhör den koncern som den svenska koncernenheten ingår i.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1374 ft2">Om en koncern har flera svenska koncernenheter ska skattskyldigheten för tilläggsskattebeloppet fördelas mellan dessa i proportion till varje enhets andel av koncernens anställda och materiella tillgångar i Sverige under det beskattningsår som tilläggsskatten avser.</P>
<P class="p1376 ft15">Om skattskyldighet enligt första stycket avser svenska koncern- enheter i olika koncerner ska</P>
<P class="p1377 ft5">tilläggsskattebeloppet för respektive koncernenhet minskas med hälften.</P>
<P class="p1378 ft3">2 b §</P>
<P class="p1376 ft3">En svensk koncernenhet som är originator är skattskyldig för hela det tilläggsskattebelopp som beräknats och fördelats på en svensk koncernenhet som är ett</P>
<P class="p1379 ft15">specialföretag för värde- papperisering. Om originatorn inte är en svensk koncernenhet är specialföretaget skattskyldigt för hela det tilläggsskattebelopp som beräknats och fördelats på detta.</P>
<P class="p1378 ft3">2 c §</P>
<P class="p1380 ft3">Med originator avses detsamma som i artikel 2.3 i Europa- parlamentets och rådets förordning (EU) 2017/2402 av den 12 december 2017 om ett allmänt ramverk för värdepapperisering och om inrättande av ett särskilt ramverk för enkel, transparent och standardiserad värdepapperisering samt om ändring av direktiven 2009/65/EG, 2009/138/EG och 2011/61/EU och förordningarna (EG) nr 1060/2009 och (EU) nr 648/2012.</P>
<P class="p1381 ft3">Med <SPAN class="ft29">specialföretag för värde-</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1382 ft5"><SPAN class="ft379">papperisering</SPAN> avses en koncernenhet</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2">
<TABLE cellpadding=0 cellspacing=0 class="t91">
<TR>
	<TD class="tr5 td39"><P class="p70 ft2">262</P></TD>
	<TD class="tr5 td699"><P class="p190 ft24"><SPAN class="ft49">6 </SPAN>Senaste lydelse 2024:1248.</P></TD>
</TR>

</DIV>
<DIV id="page_263">


<P class="p1383 ft5">1. vars verksamhet uteslutande <SPAN class="ft4">Prop. 2025/26:22 </SPAN>består i att främja genomförandet <SPAN class="ft4">Bilaga 3</SPAN></P>
<P class="p66 ft3">av en eller flera värde- papperiseringar,</P>
<P class="p63 ft3"><SPAN class="ft3">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft31">som ställer sina tillgångar som säkerhet till förmån för sina fordringsägare eller fordrings- ägare i ett annat specialföretag för värdepapperisering, och</SPAN></P>
<P class="p65 ft15"><SPAN class="ft3">3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft38">som varje år betalar ut all avkastning på tillgångarna till sina fordringsägare eller ett annat</SPAN></P>
<P class="p66 ft3">specialföretags fordringsägare förutom</P>
<P class="p63 ft3">a) ett belopp för att tillgodose ett krav enligt avtal på utdelning av vinst till andelsägarna eller motsvarande, eller</P>
<P class="p63 ft15">b) ett belopp som enligt avtal rimligen kommer att krävas för att</P>
<P class="p63 ft3">– göra avsättningar för framtida betalningar som krävs av enheten enligt avtal, eller</P>
<P class="p1384 ft15">– behålla eller förbättra enhetens kreditvärdighet.</P>
<P class="p63 ft3">En koncernenhet ska dock bara anses vara ett specialföretag för värdepapperisering om den vinst som avses i andra stycket 3 a är försumbar i förhållande till enhetens intäkter för ett visst räkenskapsår.</P>
<P class="p63 ft15">Med <SPAN class="ft48">värdepapperisering</SPAN> avses ett arrangemang som uppfyller följande förutsättningar.</P>
<P class="p63 ft3"><SPAN class="ft3">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft31">Det genomförs i syfte att sammanföra och ompaketera en portfölj av tillgångar för andra investerare än koncernenheter på ett sådant sätt att tillgångarna</SPAN></P>
<P class="p66 ft15">avskiljs från originatorns tillgångar.</P>
<P class="p67 ft3"><SPAN class="ft3">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft31">Det finns avtal som begränsar investerarnas risk vid insolvens hos den enhet som innehar de separerade tillgångarna på så sätt att övriga kända fordringsägares fordringar på enheten eller annan enhet som ingår i arrangemanget är efterställda i förhållande till</SPAN></P>
<TABLE cellpadding=0 cellspacing=0 class="t92">
<TR>
	<TD class="tr3 td700"><P class="p13 ft3">investerarnas fordringar.</P></TD>
	<TD class="tr3 td24"><P class="p16 ft2">263</P></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
</DIV>
<DIV id="page_264">

<DIV id="tx1"><SPAN class="ft9">Med </SPAN><SPAN class="ft33">skattetransparent enhet</SPAN><SPAN class="ft9"> avses en delägarbeskattad enhet till den del dess delägare är skatt- skyldiga för enhetens intäkter, kostnader, vinst eller förlust i den stat där </SPAN><SPAN class="ft16">delägaren </SPAN><SPAN class="ft9">hör hemma enligt lagstiftningen där. </SPAN><SPAN class="ft16">För att en ägare ska anses vara delägare ska den inte vara en delägarbeskattad enhet. Det krävs också att samtliga enheter under delägaren i ägarkedjan är skattetransparenta enligt lagstiftningen i den stat där ägaren hör hemma. Om samtliga ägarenheter i ägarkedjan är</SPAN></DIV>
<DIV id="tx2"><SPAN class="ft3">delägarbeskattade</SPAN><SPAN style="padding-left:72px;"><SPAN class="ft3">ska</SPAN></SPAN></DIV>
<DIV id="tx3"><SPAN class="ft4">Kompletteringsregeln ska inte tillämpas på investeringsenheter</SPAN></DIV>
<DIV id="tx4"><SPAN class="ft5">eller specialföretag för värdepapperisering</SPAN><SPAN class="ft4">.</SPAN></DIV>

<DIV id="id_1">
<DIV id="id_1_1">
<P class="p11 ft4">Prop. 2025/26:22 Bilaga 3</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_1_2">
<P class="p50 ft2">9 §</P>
<P class="p349 ft2">Om tillämpningen av 2 § om nationell tilläggsskatt och en huvudregel för tilläggsskatt i en stat inte leder till att tilläggsskattebelopp för koncernens samtliga lågbeskattade koncernenheter tas ut i sin helhet, är svenska koncernenheter skattskyldiga för kompletterande tilläggsskatt enligt bestämmelserna i <NOBR>10–13</NOBR> §§.</P>
<P class="p1385 ft4">Kompletteringsregeln ska inte tillämpas på investeringsenheter.</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>

<P class="p1388 ft2">3 §</P>
<P class="p1389 ft15"><SPAN class="ft6">Med </SPAN><SPAN class="ft48">skattetransparent enhet</SPAN><SPAN class="ft6"> avses en delägarbeskattad enhet till den del dess delägare är skatt- skyldiga för enhetens intäkter, kostnader, vinst eller förlust i den stat där </SPAN>ägaren <SPAN class="ft6">hör hemma enligt lagstiftningen där.</SPAN></P>

<DIV id="page_265">

<DIV id="tx1"><SPAN class="ft9">Med </SPAN><SPAN class="ft33">omvänd hybridenhet</SPAN><SPAN class="ft9"> avses en delägarbeskattad enhet till den del dess </SPAN><SPAN class="ft16">delägare </SPAN><SPAN class="ft9">inte är skattskyldiga för enhetens intäkter, kostnader, vinst eller förlust i den stat där delägaren hör hemma enligt lagstiftningen där. </SPAN><SPAN class="ft16">För att en ägare ska anses vara delägare ska den inte vara en delägarbeskattad enhet. Det krävs också att samtliga enheter under ägaren i ägarkedjan är skattetransparenta enligt lagstiftningen i den stat där ägaren hör hemma. Om samtliga ägarenheter i ägarkedjan är delägarbeskattade ska moder- företaget anses vara delägare.</SPAN></DIV>

<DIV id="id_1">
<DIV id="id_1_1">
<P class="p1390 ft15">moderföretaget anses vara delägare.</P>
<P class="p26 ft2">Med skattetransparent enhet avses också en koncernenhet som</P>
<P class="p26 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft44">inte har skatterättslig hemvist i någon stat,</SPAN></P>
<P class="p28 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft44">inte är skattskyldig för medräknade skatter eller för nationell tilläggsskatt på grundval av platsen för företagsledningen, platsen för bildandet eller annan liknande omständighet vad avser dess intäkter, kostnader, vinst eller förlust, och</SPAN></P>
<P class="p114 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft44">uppfyller följande förutsättningar:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p108 ft6"><SPAN class="ft2">–</SPAN><SPAN class="ft45">dess delägare hör hemma i en stat där de är skattskyldiga på det sätt som anges i första stycket,</SPAN></P>
<P class="p108 ft2"><SPAN class="ft2">–</SPAN><SPAN class="ft32">enheten har inte platsen för affärsverksamhet i den stat där den bildades, och</SPAN></P>
<P class="p108 ft4"><SPAN class="ft2">–</SPAN><SPAN class="ft50">enhetens intäkter, kostnader, vinst eller förlust kan inte hänföras till ett fast driftställe.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1391 ft2">4 §</P>
<P class="p205 ft15"><SPAN class="ft6">Med </SPAN><SPAN class="ft48">omvänd hybridenhet</SPAN><SPAN class="ft6"> avses en delägarbeskattad enhet till den del dess </SPAN>ägare <SPAN class="ft6">inte är skattskyldiga för enhetens intäkter, kostnader, vinst eller förlust i den stat där delägaren hör hemma enligt lagstiftningen där.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1392 ft2">6 §</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_1_2">
<P class="p11 ft4">Prop. 2025/26:22 Bilaga 3</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2">
<DIV id="id_2_1">
<P class="p1393 ft6">Det redovisade resultatet för en delägarbeskattad enhet ska minskas med det belopp som hör till ägare som inte är koncernenheter och som äger enheten direkt eller genom en skattetransparent struktur.</P>
<P class="p1394 ft6">Första stycket gäller inte delägarbeskattade enheter som</P>
<P class="p26 ft2"><SPAN class="ft3">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft44">är moderföretag, </SPAN><SPAN class="ft3">eller</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1393 ft4"><SPAN class="ft3">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft76">ägs, direkt eller genom en skattetransparent struktur, av ett</SPAN></P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2_2">
<P class="p58 ft2">Det redovisade resultatet för en delägarbeskattad enhet ska minskas med det belopp som hör till ägare som inte är koncernenheter och som äger enheten direkt eller <SPAN class="ft3">indirekt </SPAN>genom en <SPAN class="ft3">sådan </SPAN>skattetransparent struktur <SPAN class="ft3">som också ägs av den koncernenhet som är delägare enligt 3 eller 4 §.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p1395 ft6">Första stycket gäller inte delägarbeskattade enheter som är moderföretag. <SPAN class="ft15">Det gäller inte heller till den del en delägarbeskattad enhet </SPAN>ägs, direkt eller <SPAN class="ft15">indirekt </SPAN>genom en skattetransparent</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2_3">
<P class="p11 ft2">265</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="page_266">

<DIV id="tx1"><SPAN class="ft2">Kostnaden för </SPAN><SPAN class="ft3">andra </SPAN><SPAN class="ft2">medräknade skatter i en </SPAN><SPAN class="ft3">huvud- enhets </SPAN><SPAN class="ft2">räkenskaper </SPAN><SPAN class="ft3">än sådana som avses i 25 </SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft3">a–25</SPAN></NOBR><SPAN class="ft3"> e §§ </SPAN><SPAN class="ft2">ska fördelas till ett fast driftställe om den är hänförlig till det justerade resultatet för det fasta driftstället.</SPAN></DIV>
<DIV id="tx2"><SPAN class="ft16">Fördelning enligt första stycket ska ske med ett belopp som motsvarar huvudenhetens skatt på inkomsten från det fasta driftstället enligt lokala skatteregler i den stat där huvudenheten hör hemma,</SPAN></DIV>
<DIV id="tx3"><SPAN class="ft6">2. har redovisats i den </SPAN><SPAN class="ft15">skattetransparenta </SPAN><SPAN class="ft6">enhetens räken- skaper.</SPAN></DIV>
<DIV id="tx4"><SPAN class="ft3">Om skattekostnad fördelas till en skattetransparent enhet enligt 63 § till följd av att enheten är ett kontrollerat utländskt företag ska den fördelade skattekostnaden också omfattas av fördelning enligt första stycket. Detta gäller dock enbart om ägarenheten ägs av den koncernenhet som anges i 63 § första stycket.</SPAN></DIV>
